⚠ First month of 2026 with total spend above prior year: October total spend of $1.35M ran 29.1% above October 2025 ($1.05M), driven by CAPEX (+47.8%): a single $674K Teinert Construction General Contractor invoice at store 122 made up about 70% of the month's $958K. Facilities maintenance, by contrast, came back under prior year (-4.2%, $327K vs $342K) after two months over, while PM ran +15.9%. Work orders exceeded 2025 for a third straight month (322 vs 296, +8.8%). YTD totals remain well below 2025 — Facilities −23.1%, CAPEX −57.4%, Total −49.5%.

October highlights: Facilities maintenance came back under prior year in October (-4.2%), trimming the YTD gap to -23.1% from −24.8% in September. HVAC is essentially flat vs 2025 YTD (−1.2%). Extermination Services remains the largest overage (+18.7% YTD; $13.9K vs $9.7K in October), while Doors' overage narrowed to +12.4% after a below-prior-year October ($18.4K vs $20.6K). Fire Suppression's savings shrank to −27.5% (from −38.6%) after a $35K October vs $5.6K last year — possibly inspection timing. Equipment (+146%), Supplies (+66%), Permits (+94%), and Other (+29.8%, down from +45.7%) are %-swing items on small dollars. Racking (−89%), General Contractor (−63%), and Roofing (−47%) continue running far below 2025.

October CAPEX of $958K was dominated by one $674K Teinert Construction General Contractor invoice (store 122); Sitework ($175K) was next. That put October 47.8% above October 2025's $648K (led by $440K of New Construction) — the first month in 2026 that CAPEX exceeded prior year. YTD CAPEX remains 57.4% below 2025, so this looks like timing of one large project rather than a change in trend.
